GRAMMAR Defining relative clauses
We often use relative clauses to add information after
a noun:
He was a Czech writer who wrote about education.
You can also use that instead of who in the sentence
above.
To add information about things, use that or which.
To add information about times, use that or when.
To add information about possessions, use whose.
To add information about places, use where.
